statement_en: A set $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ is primitive if no member of $A$ divides another. Is the sum\[\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n\log n}\]maximised over all primitive sets when $A$ is the set of primes?
statement_lean:
namespace Set
def IsPrimitive (S : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  n ∈ S ∧ Disjoint (n.properDivisors : Set ℕ) S
end Set

theorem erdos_64120 :
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, (∀ a ∈ A, 2 ≤ a) → Erdos1196.IsPrimitive A →
      (∑' a : A, 1 / ((a : ℕ) * Real.log (a : ℕ))) ≤
        ∑' p : {p : ℕ | p.Prime}, 1 / ((p : ℕ) * Real.log (p : ℕ)) := by
  sorry
